# SCI-NOI v0.1 — Scientific-Owner ODQ-103 Approval

Decision identity: `SCI-NOI-ODQ-103`

Scientific owner: Grant Wilson

Decision date: `2026-08-29`

Status: scientific content approved; exact Stage-B terminology delegated

## Exact Owner Decision

> I'd approve the *scientific content* of ODQ-103 while giving the Stage-B
> scientific author freedom to find less painful terminology. The essential
> requirement is:
> **randomization is intended to suppress source signal; it does not, by
> construction alone, establish that the resulting maps are source-free.**

## Sanitized Disposition

The ordinary GEN method is designed so that its declared randomization and
balance tend to suppress astronomical source signal in the resulting
realization ensemble. That intent is part of the method definition. Neither
the randomization operation nor satisfaction of the assignment-balance design
alone establishes that an individual realization, a finite ensemble, an
ensemble average, or a derived product is source-free.

Every GEN method shall disclose the source content of its parent, the exact
suppression or cancellation target, the assumptions supporting that target,
the finite-design residual, consequential support/coefficient/projection/
filtering/selection effects, structured residuals, source-model use and error,
known or bounded leakage, and the resulting permitted and prohibited claims.

Absent separate scientific authority and evidence, a GEN product shall not be
described as a source-free null, calibrated null, repeated physical-noise
ensemble, variance, covariance, precision, significance, or detection-
probability product merely because randomization was applied.

## Terminology Delegation

The Stage-B implementation-blind scientific author may choose clearer,
scientist-readable terminology for this product and source-imprint state. The
provisional phrase `source_imprinted_conditional_randomization_ensemble` is a
nonbinding terminology suggestion, not an owner-mandated product name.

Whatever exact terminology the author selects shall preserve the approved
scientific meaning: randomization is intended to suppress source signal, but
does not by construction alone establish source-free maps. A name or shorthand
that implies guaranteed source removal, a calibrated null, physical repeated-
noise sampling, or statistical significance is not admissible.

## Non-Implications

This approval does not establish achieved source suppression, select a
numerical cancellation tolerance, make the ordinary route numerically
available, authorize a source-free or calibrated-null claim, or resolve UNC,
covariance, STD, persistence, filtering, FRUIT, VAL-profile, conformity,
validation, performance, readiness, or production questions.
